# Independent read-only review: represented command-word append

Verdict: CLEAN for final source bbe2560d7360b6776f773805aab3a1b5fe30278c4a9e32e15e5f58e65538352f and audit e75e5075cf1fd971048cd2357aff62631f7033ff284733d8a1263b973831b026. Reviewed the entire initial and final implementation, the final24-probe/30-caller audit, the actual Foundation PRF/Seq definitions and laws, and the successful run7 source/audit evidence. No Lean build or proof source edit was performed by the reviewer.

The PR.Blueprint has one actual parameter, right. Its zero state is the inner sequence[right]; successor index z is already the RAW predecessor of shifted word z+1. The successor appends replaceValue(z,znth(previous,tailValue(z)))+1 to that inner sequence. The blueprint graph order is output/previous/index/right, matching PR.Construction's actual argument convention. Public history and value graphs are ordered(out,left,right). The result graph represents the inner completed state, not the outer PR construction's sequence of states; these two levels are correctly distinguished.

All internal model indices are covered. Sequence validity and length(left+1) use definable Sigma1 induction. The bounded prefix invariant states that every i<=left entry of history(left,right) equals appendValue(i,right), rather than assuming a standard finite list interpretation. At a successor it uses actual old-entry preservation for valid sequences; the new last-entry case is definitional. Definability is justified by the fixed history and append function graphs and bounded internal quantification. No external all-relations induction or standardness assumption is substituted.

The exact recurrence then reads the earlier entry at tailValue(raw). Its bound tailValue(raw)<=raw was already proved at every IOpen input, so this read is in range. No further subtraction is used. Exterior lookups are separately proved0 using length=left+1; they do not accidentally participate in the valid recurrence. Thus the nil/MP0 distinction is preserved: shifted0 is empty; raw0 is a real command; the first nonempty shifted index is1.

appendValue_eq_zero is an internal, two-direction result: output0 iff both inputs0. It splits left using the arithmetic model's actual zero-or-successor theorem; at a successor, the represented result is replacement+1 and hence nonzero. This does not assume every model element is a standard numeral. The audit includes generic nonemptiness and zero-boundary callers.

The all-Nat append theorem uses strong induction, with tail(raw)<=raw<raw+1 giving the exact smaller input. It invokes the all-input tail/repack Nat adapters and native CommandWord254.append_succ; no quotation-only hypothesis occurs. For history_lookup_nat the final source explicitly identifies Foundation's Nat order with ordinary Nat order before rewriting the if-condition. This resolves a real instance mismatch without changing the statement or silently restricting indices. The audit covers arbitrary out-of-range lookups, both empty-word boundaries, all encoded list concatenations and the concrete1+1 word concatenation giving code6 via actual encoding lemmas.

The Sigma1 and Delta1 graphs are fixed and parameter-free. Their total unique semantics hold at all inputs of every IΣ1 model. The closed totality sentence says only that this append graph has one output for every left/right input. Completeness yields actual IΣ1 and PA provability of that same totality sentence. It is not an internal proof compiler, a command evaluator or a PA nonhalting/consistency comparison. It also does not claim every nonstandard internal code is an externally finite word.
